item.title: Braves Lock Ozzie Albies For 2027 Despite Career Lows
item.description: Dale Zanine-Imagn Images The Atlanta Braves made a move that feels wrong on paper but right for the roster. They exercised the $7 million option on Ozzie Albies for the 2027 season, according to RotoBaller MLB . This decision came even after the second baseman hit a career-low .237 last year. Per RotoBaller, the team announced the deal on Thursday, securing a player who is the franchise’s longest-tenured star. Most fans expected the team to walk away from a player who struggled so hard. Albies hit just .194 in the second half of the season with a .575 OPS. Those numbers are ugly for a guy who made four All-Star teams before. Yet the Braves paid the full price to keep him in Atlanta for one more year. His original seven-year, $35 million contract now enters its final year for the 29-year-old switch-hitter. The Math Behind The Risk Why spend $7 million on a player who missed his power and speed goals? The answer lies in his durability and the cost of replacement. Last year, Albies participated in every one of the team’s 162 regular season games. He scored 85 runs and drove in 73 while hitting 22 home runs across 615 at-bats. RotoBaller reported that he still provided plenty of value up the middle at the keystone spot. Finding a reliable everyday second baseman who can play every single game is nearly impossible in today’s league. The money also makes sense when you look at the market. A $7 million price tag for a 29-year-old with his experience is a steal. He turns 30 in January, which is still young for a veteran leader. The team avoids the risk of a free-agent bidding war or a shaky minor league call-up. They know exactly what they get: a player who shows up every day and hits for average enough to keep the lineup moving. Power Numbers Have Shifted There is a dark side to this deal that fantasy managers must watch closely. It seems Albies is no longer a threat to achieve 20 homers and 20 steals. His speed has faded, and his power has dipped below his career norms. According to the source, he recorded only a .194 average and .575 OPS during the second half. That late-season slump suggests his bat might be slowing down as he ages. Despite the drop in power, the Braves need him to stay healthy. He is the native of Curaçao who has been with the club since his debut. The organization trusts him to anchor the infield while they build around him. If he can bounce back to his .237 average from the full season, the $7 million investment pays off. If he drops below that mark, the team has no backup plan ready for 2027. The Final Year Of The Deal This move locks up the infield through 2027. Albies signed the original seven-year deal back in 2019 that included these specific options. Now he is entering the final year of that deal with the team. He will be the oldest player on the roster by experience, having reached his 10th year in the big leagues. item.title: Red-hot Evanilson finding form at the right time
item.description: Evanilson has scored five goals in all competitions this season [Getty Images] It has been a fortnight like no other for Bournemouth. Since earning a historic 3-0 victory over seven-time European champions AC Milan earlier this month, the Cherries have not looked back under new manager Marco Rose. Following that emotional night at the Vitality Stadium that underlined just how far the club has come since being plunged into administration almost 20 years ago, Rose's side have added Premier League giants Manchester United, last season's Europa League winners Aston Villa and one of the league's meanest defences, Leeds United, to their impressive resume this season. This victory against Leeds was far from vintage, with Bournemouth starting slowly and fortunate not to fall behind after Calvert-Lewin had a goal ruled out for accidental handball. But after four matches in nine days, this was a run of fixtures focused on building momentum and putting points on the board for a side with no previous experience of balancing European football with the harsh demands of the Premier League. Few have played a more prominent role in Bournemouth's four consecutive victories than Evanilson, who continued his fine form by making it four goals in as many games with a poacher's finish against Leeds. The Brazilian has enjoyed mixed fortunes on the south coast since joining Bournemouth from FC Porto in a club-record deal in 2024. However, his goal against Leeds took his total number of goal contributions this term to eight - one more than he managed during the whole of last season. Three more would see him match the 11 he managed in his impressive debut campaign, and with the Cherries flying, there is every reason to believe he can get there.

item.title: Bulls Schedule Hardens As Giddey Usage Rate Plummets
item.description: David Butler II-Imagn Images Josh Giddey is playing with fewer touches than ever, yet the Bulls offense is humming louder. While the 24-year-old guard averaged 17.0 points and 9.1 assists during his career year in 2025-26, his numbers have dipped to 7.6 points and 8.0 assists through the first five games of this season, per Pippen Ain’t Easy . The surprising twist isn’t the drop in his personal box score. It is how the team is sharing the ball while he deals with a reported wrist injury that head coach Tiago Splitter claims has not affected his play. The real story is in the usage rate. Pippen Ain’t Easy reports that Caleb Wilson and Matas Buzelis currently hold the top and third usage spots at 27.0 percent and 23.2 percent. Giddey sits at just 16.2 percent. This shift means the offense is no longer funneling everything through one player. Seven different players finished in double figures during Wednesday’s loss to the Knicks, showing that the scoring load is finally spreading out across the roster. The Knicks Game Shows Real Progress In that defeat, Chicago played a complete 48 minutes against New York, an uncommon occurrence versus a playoff-level opponent. Per Sports Illustrated , the Bulls converted 21 of 39 attempts inside the paint and earned 30 trips to the charity stripe. Even though they shot 18-42 from downtown, the ball movement was crisp. Splitter called out this specific style of play after the game. “I think we moved the ball side-to-side plenty of times, we touched the paint, sprayed the ball out, found shooters,” Splitter noted after the game. He followed up with a clear message about the team’s identity. “We finally made some shots. I think we were due for that. That’s the type of basketball we want to play. Play fast and share the ball on offense.” The coach wants this high-tempo, share-the-ball approach to become the standard, not a one-off game. Harder Tests Lie Ahead The schedule is about to get much tougher for this young squad. Norman Powell was brought in specifically for matchups like the one on Wednesday night, according to Sports Illustrated. The team faced a methodical Knicks side that knows how to slow the game down. “I thought we did a good job. That’s a good team over there. They are really methodical. They know who they want to play through. They know how to slow the game now,” Powell said. Despite the upcoming challenges, the players seem ready for the grind. Caleb Wilson is approaching the season with the right mindset. “I feel like it’s good for us to be playing these good teams so early,” Wilson said. Mandatory Credit: Patrick Gorski-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The New England Patriots have ruled out wide receiver AJ Brown for their Week 8 matchup against the Miami Dolphins. He has been dealing with an ankle and knee injury. It seems like the knee injury may have been the bigger issue this week. A.J. Brown (ankle) was downgraded from questionable to out for Sunday's game against the Dolphins. Via @RapSheet pic.twitter.com/eLeSZ1AobS - RotoWire Fantasy Football (@RotoWireNFL) October 31, 2026 This leaves the Patriots with just three wide receivers. DeMario Douglas, Efton Chism, and Kyle Williams will handle the wide receiver snaps on Sunday. Fantasy Impact WR AJ Brown, New England Patriots It's been a brutal season for Brown and his fantasy football owners. He will now miss Week 8, and there is a chance he misses more time beyond this. Many fantasy football owners had high hopes for Brown this season, but it's getting late quickly, and he has given them next to nothing in an injury-plagued year. All we can do now is monitor him as we get closer to Week 9. WR DeMario Douglas, New England Patriots Douglas is expected to step up as the Patriots' WR1 on Sunday. We've seen him have games, including Weeks 5 and 6, when he racked up a total of 11 receptions for 151 yards and three touchdowns. He becomes a sneaky good play in Week 8, but he does have a tough matchup against the Dolphins, who are allowing the third-fewest fantasy points to wide receivers this season. WR Efton Chism III, New England Patriots Chism could be a solid desperation flex option in deeper leagues this week. He is undoubtedly risky, but he should see increased volume with Brown, along with Romeo Doubs and Mack Hollins, out this week. While he is risky, he's still safer than Kyle Williams, who is a boom-or-bust option at best. TE Eli Raridon, New England Patriots The rookie tight end should have an increased role this week behind Hunter Henry, who could lead this team in receiving. He has had a role in this offense this season, including last week when he caught three passes for 56 yards and a touchdown, which was his second touchdown of the season. QB Drake Maye, New England Patriots Maye is still a locked-in QB1 this week, but when do the losses to his WR corps become too much? We are still rolling with him, but he does become much riskier with Brown being ruled out. item.title: Brooks Koepka once depicted Brandel Chamblee as a clown after finding his claim about Tiger Woods offensive
item.description: Photo by Sam Greenwood/Getty Images Brooks Koepka has never been one to mince his words. Ask him a question and you will get a straightforward answer every single time. In fact, Koepka’s honesty and uncompromising nature in general is part of his appeal. And the five-time major winner lived up to his reputation back in 2019 when Brandel Chamblee highlighted the lack of genuine challengers to Tiger Woods’ throne. Woods is unquestionably one of the two greatest golfers of all time alongside Jack Nicklaus, with 82 PGA Tour wins to his name, including 15 major championships. Meanwhile, Koepka also boasts an impressive record in the major championships, with five wins to his name The 36-year-old American has excelled in the major championships throughout his career, so it’s perhaps no surprise that he was offended by Brandel Chamblee ‘s comments back in 2019. Brooks Koepka depicted Brandel Chamblee as a clown after his Tiger Woods claim During an interview with Jaime Diaz for GOLF.com in 2019, Chamblee was asked which players were capable of ‘hanging with’ Woods when he was on top form. “In the aggregate, you’d have Dustin and Rory who are the likely two who could hang with him,” he said. “Jon Rahm’s still got a lot to learn. His iron play’s not as sharp as it needs to be to be the best player in the world, and it forces him to have to pitch the ball…his pitching, generally speaking, is not as good as it needs to be. And Spieth’s game has fallen off. So it’s really only two players who could challenge him. “Irrespective of the world rankings, I think all of us know what we need to know without the world rankings telling us, and it’s Rory and it’s Dustin Johnson and it’s Tiger Woods, but Tiger’s simply not going to play enough to get the points that he needs to get.” Koepka clearly wasn’t happy with those comments, and he took to his social media accounts to respond directly to Chamblee’s remarks. The five-time major champion posted a picture of Chamblee mocked up as a clown. The harsh reality is that nobody was a match for Tiger Woods in his prime. Whether Koepka likes it or not, Woods was on another level entirely to him. And he would surely admit that behind closed doors.

item.title: How NFL robbed Lamar Jackson’s third MVP in favour of Josh Allen, explains Rob Parker
item.description: Photo by Buda Mendes/Getty Images Rob Parker revealed that the NFL robbed Lamar Jackson of his third MVP trophy in 2024 when they awarded Josh Allen the trophy. It was the first MVP trophy for the Buffalo Bills quarterback, and it came after he threw for 3,731 passing yards on a 63.6% completion rate, while also scoring 28 passing touchdowns. His incredible season helped the Bills finish with a 13-4 record, which helped them clinch the AFC East division. Allen also had a stellar postseason run, but it ended in the AFC Championship Game after a close 32-29 defeat at the hands of the Kansas City Chiefs. Although Allen was sensational in 2024, Parker believes that the Baltimore Ravens’ Lamar Jackson was more deserving of the MVP trophy. Rob Parker believes the NFL felt sorry for Josh Allen Lamar Jackson was the reigning MVP entering the 2024 season. However, he showed no signs of slowing down and put up another monstrous year. The 29-year-old threw for 4,172 yards on a 66.7% completion rate and also had 41 passing touchdowns. He had a passer rating of 119.8, which was the best in the league. His stats indicate that this was one of his best seasons and that he had bested Allen as well. However, when it came to giving the MVP trophy, Allen was awarded the trophy, with Jackson finishing second by just 21 points. “He should have three MVPs, the best year he had in the NFL, they didn’t give him the MVP, they gave him first-team All-Pro but they gave Josh Allen the MVP cause they felt sorry for him,” Parker said on Fox’s The Odd Couple Show. Jackson’s brilliant regular season did not translate into postseason success. After winning the playoff round against the Pittsburgh Steelers, the Ravens were beaten in the AFC Divisional round by Allen’s Bills. The Bills had a narrow two-point lead going into the fourth quarter. However, it ballooned to eight points and the Ravens needed a touchdown if they were to turn things around. Jackson managed to throw a TD pass, but the Ravens failed to complete a two-point conversion, which led to a 25-27 loss. These two great QBs are set to go against each other once again on Sunday. Jackson leads the regular-season head-to-head and will look to add another win to his name on his return from injury. item.title: The clear message Anthony Edwards sent to Jaden McDaniels in T-Wolves group chat after his surgery
item.description: Photo by Stephen Maturen/Getty Images Anthony Edwards is a big miss for the Minnesota Timberwolves, but he still seems to be doing everything he can to help the team. The 25-year-old has had a lingering knee issue for a while, and the Wolves decided this week to address it through an arthroscopic procedure. The surgery was a successful one, and immediately afterwards, Edwards was on his phone to record a video for his teammates, especially Jaden McDaniels. Anthony Edwards told Jaden McDaniels to ‘step up’ in a video message Every player on the Minnesota Timberwolves roster has to step up following Edwards’ injury. Everyone’s focus will be on LaMelo Ball to guide them to victories, but the others need to play their part too, including McDaniels. The 26-year-old has had a decent start to the season, averaging 17 points and 6.5 rebounds per game, but his teammates believe he is capable of so much more. After the Wolves’ win against the Clippers in the NBA Cup, Bones Hyland had his say on McDaniels and also revealed how Edwards motivated him to step up in a video message. He said, as per Sneaker Reporter on X : “Jaden, man, I don’t think he understands how great he can be as a player. He can do everything. We always preach to Jaden, like, ‘start with you!’ “Ant sent a video to the chat yesterday, a two-minute video, just talking to us and getting us going, telling Jaden to step up more, be a leader and be the voice of the team, after a successful surgery.” Edwards is right, and his message is clear. McDaniels is not the Ant-Man , and he may never reach that level. But he is a magnificent player himself and is more than capable of stepping up and doing more for the team. The Wolves need to stay in the game until Edwards is back, and for that, they need McDaniels to contribute along with LaMelo and the rest. item.title: Leipzig sink Schalke, Fuellkrug's fine form continues
item.description: Bilal El Khannouss, a Stuttgart scorer, takes on Bayer Leverkusen defender Facundo Medina (Sascha Schuermann) RB Leipzig won 2-0 at Schalke to pick up their first away points this season, while Werder Bremen forward Niclas Fuellkrug extended his scoring run to seven straight Bundesliga games. In Gelsenkirchen, Leipzig's Antonio Nusa opened the scoring with a penalty after 37 minutes and Romulo scored 12 minutes from time to sink the promoted hosts. Leipzig, who welcome Manchester City in the Champions League on Wednesday, had won all four of their home Bundesliga matches by an 18-0 aggregate but had lost all three of their away games this season. The victory took Leipzig to fourth, one point behind third-placed Freiburg, who came from behind to win 2-1 at Augsburg. Former Freiburg forward Michael Gregoritsch put Augsburg in front after 18 minutes. The Black Forest side hit back late, with Igor Matanovic levelling things up with 65 minutes gone and Cyriaque Irie netting to put the visitors in front with five minutes remaining. In Bremen, Fuellkrug continued his remarkable scoring run since returning on a season-long loan from West Ham, grabbing the opener in a 2-0 win over Hoffenheim. Eren Dinkci also scored for Bremen but the 33-year-old Fuellkrug was the story again. By scoring in his seventh consecutive start, he equalled Rudi Voeller's club record from 1982-83. "I don't score these goals to break records," Fuellkrug said, but added the mark was "nice". "It's an absolute joy to play with this group." He has 12 goals in 10 matches in all competitions for Bremen this season, after scoring just three goals in 18 months at West Ham and one at AC Milan during a six-month loan. Ermedin Demirovic scored twice as Stuttgart broke out of a funk to win 4-2 away at in-form Bayer Leverkusen. Jamie Leweling and Bilal El Khannouss also got on the scoresheet for Stuttgart who had won just three of their previous eight matches in all competitions. In contrast, Leverkusen had won eight of their previous 10 but were cut to shreds as Stuttgart's forward line sparked to life. Patrik Schick and Ibrahim Maza scored for the hosts. Borussia Moenchengladbach continued their mini-resurgence in a 0-0 home draw with promoted Paderborn. item.title: Martinez's 'inexplicable' 83 seconds cost Man Utd and Carrick
item.description: Manchester United defender Lisandro Martinez was sent off in the second half of their 2-0 defeat at Chelsea [Getty Images] Lisandro Martinez made his way to the tunnel slowly and silently. The whistles and jeers of the Chelsea fans were ringing in his ears. Manchester United coach Jonny Evans had a brief word, but Martinez didn't pay any attention. As a player, Martinez has scaled the heights. He was part of the Argentina squad that won the World Cup in 2022 and reached the final last summer. But at Stamford Bridge, when Michael Carrick needed his side to step up and his senior players to set an example, Martinez did the very opposite. Eighteen days after Martinez called out United's summer recruitment, he suffered the kind of meltdown that would have left most United fans questioning whether that poor business involved not turfing the 28-year-old out of Old Trafford. The former Ajax defender had been part of a much-improved United performance at Chelsea, and Carrick's team should have been ahead at half-time. Even when Morgan Rogers gave the hosts a second-half lead, they had done enough for the visiting fans to believe a comeback was possible. Instead, in the space one minute and 23 seconds, Martinez committed two fouls that left Carrick's side 2-0 down and playing with 10 men - with Chelsea subsequently cruising to victory . However this woeful period unfolds, it is unlikely Martinez's recklessness will be forgotten. Martinez 'rightly sent off' Martinez was sent off with 27 minutes of normal time remaining [Getty Images] It was noticeable that Carrick did not look at Martinez as he made his way off the pitch. He was more focused on trying to come up with a plan with his assistant Steve Holland to get through the rest of the game. Asked afterwards if he felt let down by Martinez, Carrick said he had not had a chance to view the incident again. "I've not seen it back, so I don't know if it was or not," adding: "It's a big moment in the game." Carrick continued: "The second goal and losing a man at that stage had a big influence on it, for sure." For context, Martinez - already on a booking - chose the moment Estevao swung over the corner to try to block off Wesley Fofana at the far post. In the process, he raised his elbow and caught the defender in the face. The incident was missed in real time but video assistant referee (VAR) James Bell advised referee Peter Bankes to go to the screen and the obvious conclusion was reached. World Cup final official Darren Cann called Martinez's actions "inexplicable". "He jumped into him, making no attempt to play the ball and not even looking at the ball as it came in from the corner," Cann told BBC Sport. "Martinez was rightly sent off for two bookable offences, as well as conceding a needless penalty for the reckless challenge on Fofana." item.title: Khalil Mack Deal Hit A Wall As Chargers Say No Trade
item.description: Joe Nicholson-Imagn Images The Chicago Bears want Khalil Mack, but the Los Angeles Chargers are saying no. This creates a massive problem for Chicago right before the trade deadline. The Bears need help on the edge, and Mack is the perfect fix for their roster. Yet the team holding his contract refuses to sell. That is the only thing standing between Chicago and a star player. A Stubborn Roadblock The Los Angeles Chargers sit at 0-6 and have no path to the playoffs. Logic says they should trade their best players to get picks for the future. Instead, they are telling other teams that Mack is not for sale. Sports Illustrated reported on Saturday that the Chargers have “confounded teams by not engaging in trade talks.” That quote comes directly from NFL insider Jonathan Jones. This stance is baffling for everyone watching the league. The Bolts are losing every game, yet they keep Mack. Jones noted that “It’s hard to envision that remaining the case over the next 10 days.” The Bears are one of the teams trying to get him. They just traded for Jeffery Simmons to make their defense stronger. They want Mack to go with him. But the Chargers are digging in their heels. Bears Are Ready to Spend Chicago is not waiting around. General manager Ryan Poles made it clear he wants to win now. He just gave up two first-round picks to get Simmons. Poles said “from the moment we started training camp this year we were all-in.” The team is 5-2 and ready to chase a title. They have the money and the picks to make a big move. Other teams are watching closely too. On Monday, Jordan Schultz informed supporters that the Bears maintained a link to Mack interest. Ian Rapoport added that Chicago is still looking for more edge rushers after the Simmons deal. The need is real. In six games this year, Mack recorded 16 pressures and three sacks. He knows the city and played here for four years. He fits the plan perfectly. The Chargers might change their mind soon. Jones said the team is stunned by how bad the season has gone. Selling Mack makes sense before he hits free agency in 2027. The Bears have the roster to win. They just need the Chargers to finally talk. Until that happens, the deal stays dead.

item.description: Runners in the Class S boys race take to the course during the CIAC Boys Cross Country Championships held Saturday, October 31, 2026, at Wickham Park in Manchester. (Jim Shannon/Hearst Connecticut Media) Six CIAC boys cross country teams and runners will be crowned champions Saturday at Wickham Park in Manchester. Here's the rundown. Madden, Immaculate rule Class S East Granby sophomore Rockwell Madden won the small division race at the 43 rd Wickham Park XC Invitational in Manchester on Oct. 10. Three weeks later, he became a state champion for the first time. Madden won the Class S championship in 16:37.2. As he got to chute near the finish line, Madden used his fingers to display the ‘EAST GRANBY' across his jersey. "I'm not sure I would have believed it if I told myself at the beginning of the season," Madden said about winning the championship. "But after winning the invitational, that kind of helped set the state championship in my mind." In a terrific team battle, Immaculate defeated Thomaston by one point, 53-54. "We knew all season that they were the favorites going in. They're a great team with great coaching," Immaculate coach Chris Houser said about Thomaston. Christian Fappiano was the first Mustang to cross the line, taking sixth place overall in 17:09.2. Bear seniors Beau Kociszewski (16:59.8) and Braden Walker (17:06.5) finished third and fifth overall. Immaculate's finishes of fifth, seventh, 11 th , 14 th and 16 th were enough to hold off Thomaston, which took third, fourth, eighth, 19 th and 20 th . "Every one on our team PRed," Houser said, adding: "All season, they've been doing the workouts, they've been doing the right things to recover. That's where the work is." "It feels good to carry on something that's been going on for years now," Berardino said. The championship is the 14th for the Cougars, beginning in 1980. item.description: Canelo Alvarez will return to the ring this evening, challenging Christian Mbilli for the WBC super-middleweight title in Riyadh . Can Canelo prove that he is still among the best in the world? Or, as he returns from elbow surgery, will he show himself to be in the twilight of his great career? Here’s all you need to know. Per Saudi authorities, more than 300 people have been left injured and at least 21 dead, due to strikes by the Yemen-aligned Houthis. item.title: Man United sleepwalking towards relegation asks one question: Where is the rage?
item.description: As Michael Carrick walked into the press room at Stamford Bridge, with many waiting to hear whether he might actually muster some fire, there was also an eye on results elsewhere: a few permutations could have meant England’s most successful club dropped into the relegation zone at this stage of the season – now a quarter in – for the first time since 1986. That alone is a stark reality, which would be a line in the sand in any other setting. It barely needs to be said that moment in 1986 was of course when United appointed Sir Alex Ferguson . The rest is history, but this is the present and there is no sign of any salvation – from anywhere. Carrick was asked whether there was any stigma for this club to be in the relegation zone, and remarkably said “no, not for me”. You could say that was just of a piece with a bafflingly passive demeanour amid the club’s worst crisis since the actual last relegation season of 1973-74. Carrick looked a beaten man presiding over a beaten team. And consequently, it has gradually started to look like a team that can actually get relegated, too. It all looks that rotten, that broken, that structurally dysfunctional. Chelsea didn’t even have to be good in this 2-0 win, as witnessed in the opening goal. Morgan Rogers was allowed to run in a straight line through the defensive structure of the United team. It was remarkable to see that at this level of football. There was then the entire Lisandro Martinez episode, the defender getting a second booking for the match-settling penalty after what must have been one of the most dismal 10 minutes for a player of that level in modern Premier League history. As Carrick was further pressed on what being in the relegation zone might actually mean, he merely went on: “You can move up the league quite quickly if you win football matches.” Except, United don’t look like doing that any time soon. They haven’t won in nine, their worst run since 1988. While there’s been a lot of focus on Carrick’s demeanour and how a measured approach that used to be considered a strength now looks a weakness, it’s hard to see how there couldn’t be more fury at this. To paraphrase a line that has become a meme, this is Manchester United in a relegation battle we’re talking about. One of their greatest ever servants should be furious. What standards are these? What would he have to lose by blasting Martinez at this point? Such a display makes Carrick look like what many feel he is: a place-holder. United’s leadership haven’t had the decisiveness or maybe football intelligence to make the call to sack him. And yet for all that Carrick is the focus, and will inevitably be the one to lose his job from all this, there is of course a much wider story. item.title: Jessie Bates III Praises Matt Ryan’s Hands-On Role With Falcons
item.description: Brett Davis-Imagn Images The Atlanta Falcons have a new voice in the front office, and the players are already taking notice. Jessie Bates III, the team’s starting safety, opened up about former quarterback Matt Ryan’s new job as President of Football. During an appearance on the “Pat McAfee Show” on Friday, Bates said Ryan is doing more than just making calls from an office. He is out on the practice field every day, helping players fix their technique and understand the game. Bates, 29, admitted that Ryan’s presence has already helped the team improve. The Falcons are 3-4 as they head into Week 8, but the players feel a shift in the culture. Ryan knows exactly what it takes to succeed because he played most of his career for this franchise. He is not just a suit in a suit; he is a football guy who knows the grind. A Coach in Disguise Ryan’s approach is direct and practical. He does not wait for coaches to come to him. He goes to the players. Bates told the media that Ryan is throwing deep balls to receivers and showing them how to drop back against modern defenses. This level of detail usually comes from a position coach, not an executive. “You’d think he’s our safety position coach,” Bates continued, according to Yahoo Sports . Nowadays these quarterbacks see him go out there and occasionally throw a deep ball, offering a solid look across various drops; he remains hands-on. This is not just about football skills. It is about trust. When a former player who knows the system takes a leadership role, the younger guys listen. They know he has been in their shoes. He knows the pressure of the NFL. This helps the team stay focused during a long season. Handling the Daily Grind Former Falcon Roddy White sees the same thing. White, who spent his entire 11-year career in Atlanta, has watched Ryan handle the new job with care. White noted that the role is hard. There are many tasks to do every single day. Ryan has to manage the roster, the cap, and the coaching staff all at once. “It’s a very challenged job, just having everything that you have to do on a day-to-day basis,” White said. “He’s always going to be a guy that’s always in as far as being on the field, watching, paying attention, the players and seeing where they are at, because he’s done it before.” White pointed out that Ryan’s work ethic is the key.
